description: READ BACK A LINE OF REASONING, read-only: an argument for and against, an experiment's case, a paper's chain of claims, a legal case. Each claim comes with its COMPUTED truth (holds, fails or unknown), the steps that support it (rule, warrant, who confirmed them), the objections against it and how each stands (`refutes`, `stands`, `answered`), and its cited sources. Then: what the reasoning rests on and which premises cite no source, the points still contested, the disputes a Decision set to `contested` keeps open on purpose, and every claim with no support. `claim` reads under one claim; omitted, every top conclusion and contested decision. `what_this_means`: structure is not truth. Shown here, never raised as a gap. Bounded by `budget_chars`. Writes nothing. Ask for this to check an argument point by point: what backs each claim, what is disputed, and what has no evidence behind it.

budget_chars.description:
Characters the reply may spend (default 30,000). Over it, the claims'
prose gives first, then claims from the end of the walk; every summary
list keeps its ids, and the `budget` block says what was withheld.

claim.description:
The claim to read the reasoning under: its support, what it rests on
and what stands against it, all the way down. Omitted: every top
conclusion (a node a step concludes that supports nothing further) and
every Decision set to `contested`.

limit.description:
How many nodes to read (default 60, at most 500). `capped: true` in
the reply means the walk stopped before reaching everything.

name: reasoning_report
title: Reasoning Report
